title: Dedicated surge confinement and adaptive credit decay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A dedicated cluster capacity event on 2026-02-18 produced rapid eviction storms and cascading tail latency for several tenant workloads. Root cause analysis showed a combination of (a) skewed reservation estimates for a small set of tenants, (b) a burst policy that allowed large instantaneous token consumption without graceful decay, and (c) KV-cache pressure that gave no priority differentiation between short-lived interactive requests and long-running streaming jobs.

Objective: Implement a coordinated mitigation strategy that confines surges, reduces eviction probability, and prevents reoccurrence by: (1) introducing an adaptive credit-decay algorithm to dampen burst tokens over time, (2) adding KV-cache priority lanes to protect latency-sensitive tenants, and (3) scheduling a nightly reservation-shadowing job to detect and auto-suggest reservation right-sizing.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Eviction rate in dedicated pools drops by >= 80% in post-deploy synthetic surge tests (compare baseline from 2026-02-18 incident).
- 95th percentile latency for interactive tenants remains within pre-incident SLO under 5x synthetic ramp.
- Reservation-suggested deltas generated by shadowing job are produced and logged for 100% of tenants within 24h of job run.
- Canary rollout completes to 25% of clusters with no customer-facing degradations and no automated rollback triggers.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change long-term billing model or customer-visible quota UI. It focuses on infrastructure controls and internal autoscaler logic.

Proposed implementation (high level):
- Adaptive credit decay: replace current fixed-burst allowance with a weighted leaky-bucket per-tenant where decay rate is a function of recent 1h/6h consumption percentiles and reservation headroom. Include backoff hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- KV-cache priority lanes: implement two soft lanes (latency, throughput). Latency lane gets reserved small KV memory region and is favored for prefix/KV cache hits; throughput lane degrades to eviction sooner during pressure. Expose per-tenant policy flag for lane preference determined by customer tier and config.
- Reservation shadow job: daily job that computes moving-average per-tenant qps and tail token consumption, writes suggested reservation delta to a proposal table and produces a PRD-style CSV for SRE/PM review.
- Telemetry & synthetic validation: add Grafana panels and synthetic scenarios to the chaos lab to validate behavior across burst sizes and KV pressure.

Rollback plan: Server side feature gating with cluster-level flags. Immediate rollback: flip gating to false, revert autoscaler tuning commit.
